contract: construct(instance) -> array of shape (n, 3): Cartesian coordinates of n atoms in reduced units. instance = {'potential': 'dzugutov', 'n': atoms, 'A', 'B', 'a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'm'}; called once for each n in (38, 45, 50, 55, 57, 60); all calls together within 300 s (enforced) and should use at most 4 threads (not enforced by the evaluator). The evaluator recomputes E = sum_{i<j} V(r_ij) with V(r) = A(r^-m - B)exp(c/(r - a)) [r < a] + B exp(d/(r - b)) [r < b], A = 5.82, B = 1.28, a = 1.87, b = 1.94, c = 1.10, d = 0.27, m = 16; atoms must be at least 0.5 apart. Score: mean over instances of 100*(E - E_pub)/|E_pub| against the putative global minima of Doye, Wales and Simdyankin (2001) (minimize; 0 matches all six, negative is lower). chem_clusters.relax(positions, 'dzugutov') and chem_clusters.dzugutov_energy_gradient(positions) may be called
notes: Pair potential recomputed without further cutoff beyond its own smooth cutoffs at a and b. Reference check (tests/test_chem_clusters.py): the relaxed 7-atom pentagonal bipyramid and 13-atom icosahedron reproduce the published minima within six decimals. The authors note that minima above about 60 atoms may be improvable, so only sizes up to 60 are scored.

name: Dzugutov cluster global minima (polytetrahedral model metal)
description: Find the lowest-energy structures of 38- to 60-atom clusters bound by the Dzugutov potential, a model of glass- and quasicrystal-forming metals whose energy maximum favours polytetrahedral order (six instances). Energies are recomputed exactly and compared with the putative global minima of Doye, Wales and Simdyankin.

sources.locator: Doye, Wales and Simdyankin (2001): Dzugutov potential parameters and table of putative global minima for N = 3-100 (arXiv cond-mat/0011018).
Dzugutov (1992): the pair potential designed to suppress crystallisation in a monatomic liquid.
LaTeX source of the global-minimum table (six decimals).

limitations: The references are 2001 putative minima; the authors note that sizes above about 60 may have lower minima, so only sizes up to 60 are used, and the Cambridge Cluster Database listed the same six energies on 2026-11-24 (its coordinate files score them with this evaluator within 5e-7).
Putative minima are public, so remembered structures score well without search.
The score averages relative energy excesses over six instances within a shared 300 s budget.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Find the lowest-energy structure of an atomic cluster for a given interatomic potential (global optimisation on a rugged energy landscape). Here: clusters of the Dzugutov potential, a model of glass- and quasicrystal-forming metals.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Polytetrahedral order underlies metallic glasses, Frank-Kasper phases and quasicrystals; the global minima of Dzugutov clusters show which polytetrahedral structures such systems favour.
